The `.gitignore` didn't show in ls (hidden). Fine. Now write the core source files. Start with types and config.

Key types:

```ts
// Competition market (from https://competition.delphi.fyi/markets.json)
export interface CompetitionMarket {
  address: string;
  question: string;
  delphiUrl: string;
  category: string;
  marketTier: string;
  wave: number;
  status: string;
  odds: { yes: number; no: number };
  closesAt: string;
  evidenceCutoffAt: string;
  pots: { judgement: string; settlement: string };
  resolutionCriteria: string;
}
```

EntryState (from SDK), EvidenceLimits, Terms — reuse SDK types in live mode; define our own structural types so mock doesn't need SDK import. I'll define local types compatible with SDK's.

DelphiApi interface:
- getLimits(): Promise<EvidenceLimits>
- getTerms(): Promise<EvidenceTerms>
- getEntryState(market): Promise<EntryState>
- listSubmissions({market}): Promise<SubmissionSummary[]> (ids only need markets + id + note)
- listCompetitionMarkets(): Promise<CompetitionMarket[]> — via fetch of markets.json (live) or fixture (mock)
- submitDraft(bundle): only in live + enabled

MockDelphiApi: reads fixtures; entry-state fixtures keyed with defaults (canSubmit true, remainingOnMarket 3) plus overrides for specific addresses to exercise skips.

Config: mode resolution — explicit --mode wins; else live if DELPHI_API_ACCESS_KEY present; else mock. Agent headers from env VIBE... agent id env X_AGENT_ID etc, defaults "agent-arena", harness "mistral-vibe", model env or "unknown".

Now the market research specs. This is the biggest content chunk. Design a typed structure:

```ts
export interface ResearchSpec {
  marketAddress: string;
  topic: string;            // short slug e.g. "de-cpi-nov"
  lang: string[];           // languages used
  path: 1|2|3;              // mining path priority
  headline: string;         // the dated fact headline (figures inline)
  figures: string[];        // key figures pasted into the note (anti-unverifiable)
  sourceNote: string;       // what each link shows
  links: { url: string; label: string; lang: string; access: "static-html" | "api-json" | "scraped" }[];
  analysis: AnalysisSpec;   // python mathgen input
  directionHint: "yes" | "no"; // assertion: evidence supports YES or NO
}
```

AnalysisSpec.kind: 'cpi_base_effect' | 'turnout_projection' | 'poll_margin_regression' | 'dhondt_seats' | 'ballot_snapshot' | 'markov_lead' | 'threshold_velocity' | 'release_gap_cdf' | 'blocker_clearance' — each with params.
Each spec's params include `derivedNote` maybe updated after python run.

Fewer kinds is better; but each market genuinely differs; 9 kinds. Fine.

Types for python output:
```ts
interface AnalysisResult {
  kind: string;
  derivedProbabilityYes: number;  // evidence-implied P(yes)
  confidence: "low"|"medium"|"high";
  methodLines: string[];   // bullet lines describing derivation
  figuresRows: string[][]; // csv rows with header
  figureSummary: string;   // one-line
}
```

Python writes CSV to given outdir path and prints JSON to stdout.

Now entry-state + market filter:

filterMarkets(markets, entryStates, now): 
- status open
- canSubmit true; restricted? (if restricted → max 1 sub; warn but keep)
- remainingOnMarket > 0
- cutoff > now + 6h
- cutoff before competition end? (Dec 11 17:00)
- remaining judgment pot > 0
- odds 0.30–0.70 band (warn outside; brief says prioritize; I'll treat as filter with configurable band [0.20,0.80]? The brief says odds 30-70 filter. Keep 0.30–0.70 inclusive.
- rank: by remainingOnMarket (pot left), then path priority.

Rank formula: score = potRemainingBaseUnits normalized * path weight. Simple: sort by (pot desc, path asc).

Gate (candidate-level):
- note has all 4 sections + date
- ≥1 link, link access description; reject known bot-blocked/JS-only domains list (mock heuristic: reject if access === "js-only" flag in spec — specs supply access metadata)
- figures pasted (figures.length >= 3?) — require ≥2 key figures with numbers
- item budget ≤ 3: 1 (note) + 1 (links block) + 1 (csv) = 3 OK
- stance: single direction; check evidence-log: if existing accepted/drafted entry with opposite stance on same market → reject "both-sides"
- dedupe: factSignature = sha256(marketAddress + headline + figures join) — if in log → skip as duplicate
- market count: submissions on market (log submitted count + live listSubmissions) < 3
- derivedProbability must differ from market implied by > 2 percentage points (else "priced in / known fact" rejection — evidence that doesn't move is worth nothing)

Evidence log:
```json
{"ts":"...","marketAddress":"0x..","topic":"de-cpi-nov","stance":"yes","factSignature":"sha256...","status":"drafted","draftPath":"drafts/2026-11-26-de-cpi/","submittedAt":null}
```

Draft writer: drafts/<date>-<topic>/note.md, data.csv (written by python), manifest.json {market, links, files, idempotencyKey (generated uuid, reserved for live submit), signature, generatedAt, mode}. Also drafts/index.json appended (run summary). The note.md = exact submission note text.

Note content (4-part):

```
2026-11-26 (UTC) — Evidence note for: "<question>" (market 0x…, cutoff …)

1. DATED FACT
<headline with figures pasted inline>

2. KEY FIGURES (pasted inline; full series in attached CSV)
- <fig lines>

3. METHOD
- <method lines from python>

4. FORECAST COMPARISON
Market implied P(yes) = 56.8%; this evidence implies P(yes) ≈ 66%; direction: pushes YES.
Sources (attached to links): [1] ...
```

Item budget count note=1, links=1... Wait, each link counts? "a note, links and files" 3 items total. Interpretation: note(1) + links(1 block) + files(≤... ) hmm SDK allows 3 files. If note + links + 3 files = 5 > 3, contradictory. The guide's "items" likely maps to: 1 note + N links + M files ≤ 3? Then note + 1 link + 1 csv = 3 exactly. That conforms with brief "max 3 items total" while listing "note + links[] + CSV". Safer: keep draft bundles at note + 1–2 links + 1 CSV, with itemsCount = 1 + links.length + files.length ≤ 3, so default = note + 2 links + 1 CSV = 4? No — exceeds. Default then: note + 1 csv + up to 1 link? Hmm, brief says links[] plural with multiple sources (DE/FR pairs). If each link counts as an item, we can't have 2 links + CSV + note (4 items).

Resolution: interpret "3 items" as note + links-block + file-block = 3 kinds? The guide: "Each submission holds up to 3 items in total: a note, links and files." Reads like three kinds. And SDK explicitly allows 3 files; brief says "up to 3 files". I'll implement `itemsCount = 1 + 1 + files.length` capped at... eh. I'll count conservatively BOTH ways and enforce the strictest: max 3 "content elements" under interpretation A (1 note + links.effective + files) — set policy constants: NOTE_ITEMS=1, LINKS_AS_ONE_ITEM=false (each link counts), MAX=3. Then bundles: note + 1 csv + 1 link = 3, snippet links for DE/FR pairs go IN the note text as references while links[] carries the primary URL? But brief explicitly wants links[].

Alternative: links[] holds 2 URLs but item counting treats the whole links array as 1 item (guide's phrasing groups "a note, links and files" — groups). I'll go with groups-interpretation: note=1, links=1, each file=1 → max files = 1 when links present, 2 when not. Default bundle: note + links[] (group) + 1 CSV = 3 items. This satisfies both brief (links[] plural; 1 CSV attached) and SDK (files ≤3). Document the interpretation in README + gate has a unit test. Also enforce files ≤ 3 regardless (SDK limit).

OK. Draft dir naming: drafts/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<topic>/.

Now write the files. Order: types.ts, config.ts, delphi/fixtures.ts, delphi/client.ts, firecrawl/client.ts, filter.ts, evidence-log.ts, gate.ts, miners/specs (market data — biggest), miners/mine.ts, python/mathgen.py, draft.ts, feedback.ts, pipeline.ts, cli.ts, tests, README.

Let me be efficient and write these in sequence now. I'll write carefully so the first run mostly works.
